title: Drum lessons from Louis Cottrell
summary: He studied with Cottrell for six or seven months at about eighteen, after already playing in organised groups; Cottrell's later records with Piron are mentioned.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I've taken my drum lesson from Cottrell. Lewis Cottrell.
Did you tell us more about him?

Well, all I know is he's one of the finest drummers around the city of New Orleans, I can tell you that. That's what everybody said. Played with Excelsior Brass, brass man. Yeah, it was techno. How long did you go to him? All about a few months, six, seven months until he passed.
But at the end of his life, when was that? Do you remember when he died? We'll get that information from his son, of course.
Well, I was wondering, how old were you when he died? You might know roughly.
Oh, I just can't say no one year that was then. One more year. The only one I can tell, that's his son, his son, Lewis. Yeah, he'll tell us his son. Yeah, he'll tell us his son.
Yeah, he'll tell us his son. Well, actually, you were pretty much a grown man before you took drum lessons.
Well, I was, let's see, in the 20s. I was around 18 years old, sure.
Before you took lessons from him, huh? And then, let's see, well, he made records in 24. He made that in New York.
Oh, with Pierron. Oh, yeah, they played, they made this recording of Sister Kate. They had West Vietnamese Blues. Anybody want to buy my cabbage? That's the recording they made of.
Yeah, they made quite a few out there.
Yeah, they have a lot of them.
So he must have died after he came back here.
Oh, yeah, after he came from New York, yeah.
Were you playing long before you took lessons from him?
Well, I was playing with all the organized groups, you know. Before you ever took any lessons? Yeah, before I was taking them.
